content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 15
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 19

---

## V.2 — "the all-seeing" vs. "the All-seeing" vs. "the All-seeing"
- EMET: lowercase "all-seeing"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: capitalized as a divine title
- SOPHIA: capitalize — *panepoptēs*: the All-seeing is used as a divine name/title in 2 Maccabees; capitalize

## V.3 — "thrice-accursed wretch" vs. "thrice-accursed wretch" vs. "three-times-cursed wretch"
- EMET/LOGOS: "thrice-accursed"
- PNEUMA: "three-times-cursed" (literal but less idiomatic)
- SOPHIA: "thrice-accursed wretch" — the traditional expression is more forceful

## V.5 — "carry out the king's business" vs. "carry out the king's orders" vs. "carry out the king's business"
- EMET/PNEUMA: "king's business"
- LOGOS: "king's orders"
- SOPHIA: "king's orders" — Greek *ta tou basileōs epitattō*: I command the king's commands; "orders" more precise

## V.6 — "utter boastfulness and arrogance" vs. "utter arrogance and presumption" vs. "arrogance and pride"
- EMET: "boastfulness and arrogance"
- LOGOS: "arrogance and presumption"
- PNEUMA: "arrogance and pride"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — Greek *hyperēphania kai alazoneia*: arrogance and presumption/boastfulness

## V.8 — "former help" vs. "previously received help" vs. "all the times heaven had come to their aid"
- EMET: "former help"
- LOGOS: "help they had previously received"
- PNEUMA: expands to "all the times heaven had come to their aid"
- SOPHIA: "help they had previously received" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's expansion is paraphrase

## V.9 — "struggles they had already come through" vs. "battles they had already won" vs. "battles they had already won"
- LOGOS: "struggles" (*agōnes*: contests/struggles)
- EMET/PNEUMA: "battles...won" (more specific)
- SOPHIA: "battles they had already won" — contextually these were military engagements; EMET/PNEUMA preferred

## V.11 — "a sort of vision" vs. "a kind of waking vision" vs. (no qualifier)
- EMET: "a sort of vision"
- LOGOS: "a kind of waking vision" (adds "waking")
- PNEUMA: omits the qualifying phrase
- SOPHIA: "a sort of waking vision" — Greek *horama*: vision; the modifier hedges the category

## V.12 — Onias description: PNEUMA condenses; EMET/LOGOS retain all epithets
- PNEUMA omits "gracious in speech" and condenses the description
- SOPHIA: retain all epithets — the author's elaborate ekphrasis is deliberate

## V.14 — "loves the brethren" vs. "loves the family of Israel" vs. "loves the brotherhood"
- EMET: "brethren"
- LOGOS: "family of Israel" (adds "Israel" — interpretive expansion)
- PNEUMA: "brotherhood"
- SOPHIA: "his brethren" — Greek *tōn adelphōn philoprostatēs*: defender/lover of the brethren

## V.16 — "strike down your adversaries" vs. "shatter your adversaries" vs. "shatter your enemies"
- EMET: "strike down"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "shatter"
- SOPHIA: "shatter" — Greek *paipakseis*: will strike/smite/shatter; LOGOS's "shatter" captures the violence

## V.17 — "make the young men's souls strong" vs. "fortifying the courage of the young" vs. "make young men brave"
- EMET: "make the young men's souls strong"
- LOGOS: "fortifying the courage of the young"
- PNEUMA: "make young men brave"
- SOPHIA: EMET — "young men's souls" retains the *psychē* (soul) reference

## V.18 — "greatest and chief fear" vs. "greatest and first concern" vs. "what gripped them most"
- EMET: "greatest and chief fear"
- LOGOS: "greatest and first concern"
- PNEUMA: "what gripped them most"
- SOPHIA: "greatest and foremost concern" — *meizōn de kai prōtē phrontis*: greater and first/foremost concern

## V.21 — "works wonders" — all three agree
- Greek *teratōn poiētēn*: maker of wonders/miracles; all three render correctly

## V.22 — "sent your angel" — all three agree on Hezekiah reference
- EMET/LOGOS: "a hundred and eighty-five thousand"
- PNEUMA: "185,000" (numeral)
- SOPHIA: spell out — "a hundred and eighty-five thousand"

## V.27 — "manifestation of God" vs. "manifestation of God" vs. "what God had done"
- EMET/LOGOS: "the manifestation of God" (*epiphaneia*)
- PNEUMA: "what God had done" (loses the technical *epiphaneia* term)
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS — the *epiphaneia* language is the theological signature of 2 Maccabees

## V.33 — "feed it to the birds bit by bit" vs. "give it piecemeal to the birds" vs. "give it to the birds in pieces"
- EMET: "bit by bit"
- LOGOS: "piecemeal"
- PNEUMA: "in pieces"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "piecemeal" is the clearest

## V.36 — "the day before Mordecai's day" — all three agree
- The reference to Purim; all three correctly identify it
- Note: "Mordecai's day" = Purim; 13 Adar = Nicanor's Day; 14 Adar = Purim

## V.38 — "cheap and mediocre" vs. "poor and mediocre" vs. "inadequate and falls short"
- EMET: "cheap and mediocre" (*phaulon kai mediokron*)
- LOGOS: "poor and mediocre"
- PNEUMA: "inadequate and falls short"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "poor and mediocre" captures both Greek terms; EMET's "cheap" is slightly harsh; PNEUMA loses the rhetorical self-deprecation

## V.39 — Closing wine-water simile: all three render it; PNEUMA expands
- EMET: most literal; "cheap" for *phaulon*
- LOGOS: balanced formal rendering
- PNEUMA: natural, conversational — "You know how it is with wine"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS structure with slightly more natural English; the simile must be preserved in full
